analysis.investment_thesis: EIH's Oberoi brand is among India's finest luxury hospitality assets — commanding operating margins of 38.9% and an almost debt-free balance sheet (D/E 0.05) that I deeply respect. However, promoter holding of just 32.85% is a serious governance concern for me, COVID revealed the brutal cyclicality of hospitality (net losses of –INR 375 Cr and –INR 95 Cr in FY21-22), and the P/E of 26.5x prices in a lot of the recovery already.
key_strengths: Virtually debt-free balance sheet — D/E of 0.05x with net cash positive (INR 378 Cr cash vs INR 265 Cr debt) — one of the cleanest balance sheets in hospitality globally
Operating margins of 38.9% reflect exceptional brand pricing power; luxury hospitality with this margin structure is a rare and genuine moat
Aggressive post-COVID deleveraging: borrowings fell from INR 647 Cr (FY20) to INR 199 Cr (FY24), showing capital discipline even in difficult times
key_risks: Promoter holding of only 32.85% is the single largest concern — I need promoters with significant skin in the game, and this level suggests meaningful historical dilution
COVID demonstrated catastrophic earnings vulnerability — OCF was negative in FY21 and FY22, and net losses totalled INR 470 Cr over two years; this can happen again
Capex is accelerating sharply (INR 485 Cr in FY25 vs INR 67 Cr in FY22) with CWIP at INR 403 Cr — expansion at peak cycle valuations raises the risk of capital allocation error
red_flags: Promoter holding of 32.85% is far below my 55% minimum — this is the most significant red flag and prevents a higher rating regardless of business quality
OCF was negative in 2 of the last 5 years — I require consistency of cash generation, and hospitality structurally cannot provide it
P/S of 6.88x and P/E of 26.5x on a business with 5.7% revenue CAGR over 9 years is pricing perfection into a cyclical business
analysis.detailed_analysis:
I have enormous respect for the Oberoi brand — it represents India's finest luxury hospitality and commands genuine pricing power that shows up in those 38.9% operating margins. The balance sheet stewardship has been excellent: D/E has collapsed from 0.2x post-COVID to 0.05x today, and cash generation in the post-COVID recovery (OCF: INR 614 Cr → INR 825 Cr) has been strong. This is a quality business being managed conservatively on the liability side.

But I cannot overlook the promoter holding at 32.85%. When I built DMart, I retained control because I believed in the business absolutely — low promoter holding signals something has changed in the founder's conviction. Add to that the inherent cyclicality of hospitality (COVID wiped two years of profits), rising capex at peak-cycle multiples, and a P/E of 26.5x that already prices in the recovery, and I prefer to watch from the sidelines. Current holders with a long-term horizon can stay, but fresh capital has better homes.
